name: Later Han (Five Dynasties)
alt: Later Han of the Five Dynasties

predecessors.name: Later Jin
predecessors.text: the Later Jin realm: the Later Han 'held essentially the same territory as the Later Jin'

predecessors.name: Liao dynasty (Great Khitan State)
predecessors.text: the Central Plain the Khitan left: Emperor Taizong of Liao's force reached the Yellow River, then turned back toward his base near present-day Beijing

successors.name: Later Zhou
successors.text: the Later Han realm without the Northern Han core in Shanxi (Guo Wei's realm at Kaifeng)

successors.name: Northern Han
successors.text: the Shanxi core where the Northern Han began: 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi'

ledger.x: 947: Liu Zhiyuan takes over the Central Plain from the Khitan.
947: the Later Han capital moves from Taiyuan to Bian (Kaifeng).
10 March 947: Liu Zhiyuan proclaims the Later Han at Taiyuan.
951: the Northern Han splits off in Shanxi.
January 951: Guo Wei takes the realm at Kaifeng.
1-2 January 951: the Later Han ends in Guo Wei's coup.

wars.name: Khitan withdrawal from the Central Plain and the rise of the Later Han
wars.outcome: The Liao force that had taken Kaifeng reached the Yellow River and turned back; Taizong of Liao died in May 947 and Liu Zhiyuan filled the vacuum, keeping the Sixteen Prefectures with the Liao.

wars.name: Guo Wei's coup against the Later Han
wars.outcome: General Guo Wei seized Bian on 1-2 January 951 and was proclaimed emperor of the Later Zhou on 13 February 951; the Later Han remnants returned to Shanxi as the Northern Han.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Later Han border; the page describes the south as a line 'about halfway between the Yellow and Yangtze rivers' and the northern frontier with the Liao follows the Sixteen Prefectures, which are not surveyed…
